title: A tree of life (Proverbs 3:17–18)
hookLine: sung as the Torah returns to the ark: "Her ways are ways of pleasantness, and all her paths are peace"

lines: THE SCROLL RETURNS TO THE ARK.
cards: The reading is over. The scroll has been lifted, rolled and dressed again in its cover. It's carried back toward the ark at the front of the synagogue, and the doors stand open.
As it goes in, the congregation sings. The song's opening lines aren't new words written for the moment. They're two verses lifted straight out of the book of Proverbs.
Wisdom and Torah, sung in one breath, and then the doors close on the scroll.

teach.b: Here they are, in the King James words: "She is a tree of life to them that lay hold upon her." And just before it: "Her ways are ways of pleasantness, and all her paths are peace."
In Proverbs, the she is wisdom, described like a person: more precious than rubies, long life in one hand, riches and honor in the other.

Then the synagogue does something quiet and bold: it sings those verses about the Torah. The Torah becomes the tree, and the people singing are the ones holding on. Notice the verb: lay hold upon her.

teach.h: SHE IS A TREE OF LIFE.
teach.b: A tree of life isn't admired from a distance. You grab it. The tradition gives this a physical shape too: the wooden rollers a Torah scroll is wound on are called atzei chayim, trees of life.
Every time someone lifts the scroll, their hands are literally on the trees.
And her ways are ways of pleasantness became a test for some Jewish teachers: in the Talmud, a reading of the law that would bring needless hardship is set aside, because her ways are pleasant.
All her paths are peace. Peace here is shalom, a word with room in it for wholeness, for things being as they should be.
So the song asks a lot of the people who sing it: hold on to the tree, and choose the path that leads to peace.

how: In synagogue services, as the Torah scroll is returned to the ark, congregations sing Etz chayim hi, the verses from Proverbs 3:18 and 3:17, before the ark is closed.

o: the cloth cover a Torah scroll is dressed in
the open doors of the ark in a synagogue
trees of life, the wooden rollers of a Torah scroll

games.q: all her paths are peace — tap the pairs.

s: the song at the ark opens with words written for the service
its opening words come straight from Proverbs 3:17–18.
the wooden rollers of a Torah scroll are called trees of life
atzei chayim: so whoever lifts the scroll holds the trees.
in Proverbs, the 'she' of these verses is wisdom
the chapter describes wisdom like a person; the synagogue sings it of the Torah.

games.q: the reading is done and the scroll is carried back to the ark. what does the congregation do?
games.why: they sing: she is a tree of life to them that lay hold upon her, and all her paths are peace.

practice: Let one choice from today come to mind, a message to answer, a chore, a conversation, a line at the store, and picture two ways through it, one sharper, one gentler, without deciding yet.
Then let your hands close lightly, as if holding on to something steady. If you pray, you can say the line silently, all her paths are peace; if not, just breathe and hold the picture.

wordCard.voice: atzei chayim, trees of life, the name for the wooden rollers a Torah scroll is wound on and lifted by. Today's word.

orig.note: Hebrew: tree of life, from Proverbs 3:18, and the name for a Torah scroll's rollers.

carryVoice: Your line: all her paths are peace. Wisdom, Torah and a tree, all in one song. See you tomorrow.
